One element of the Nvidia imbroglio is a little-known but powerful Commerce Department agency that’s known as the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and falls under Lutnick’s jurisdiction.

BIS regulates exports of a wide range of products — including advanced AI chips — and it’s set to face renewed scrutiny as lawmakers threaten probes into the bureau’s leader, Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler.

The Senate Banking committee is already planning inquiries into Lutnick and Kessler’s decision-making. The two men “must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military,” Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the committee, said in a statement.

In late summer 2025, Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter called Kessler to ask whether BIS was involved in the Singapore government’s recent detention of Alice Huang, Bloomberg News reported this week. BIS was not involved in that action, Bloomberg reported earlier, citing people familiar with the matter.

An Nvidia spokesperson has said that Teter was unaware of the affair at the time he called Kessler about Alice Huang’s detention in Singapore. But in the weeks following the call, BIS staff were muzzled in their ability to investigate the company, including a mandate that they route all request of Nvidia through Kessler, Bloomberg reported.

“It’s really important to understand what the Commerce Department knew about Megaspeed,” said Ben Buchanan, former White House special adviser for AI during the Biden administration, in a Bloomberg Television interview. “This is an incident where the enforcement is not good. The decision making has not been good.”

title: Asda’s flat sales end losing streak as new CEO joins UK grocer
article:
(Nov 13): Asda avoided a quarterly drop in sales for the first time in more than two years — though just barely — as the struggling grocer drew more shoppers online with the help of its loyalty programme.

Comparable sales excluding fuel edged up 0.1% in the 13 weeks to Sept 30, the UK’s third-largest supermarket chain said on Friday, snapping a run of nine consecutive quarters of declines. Online grocery sales rose 6.9%.

The results will offer some encouragement as new chief executive officer David Potts, who was appointed last week, tries to revive a business that’s lost market share since it was acquired in a highly leveraged buyout in 2021.

Asda faces a highly competitive UK grocery market in which the likes of Tesco plc, J Sainsbury plc, and German discounters Aldi and Lidl have eaten into its customer base. Its market share is 11.3%, according to the latest data from market tracker Worldpanel by Numerator, down from 14.3% at the start of 2021.

That was the year Asda was acquired from Walmart Inc by British billionaire brothers Mohsin and Zuber Issa alongside private equity firm TDR Capital, which has since become the majority shareholder.

Asda’s debt burden since that deal hindered turnaround efforts, as did a botched IT overhaul related to the separation from Walmart’s systems.

See also: Poundland files to delay UK insolvency as it finds a rescuer

The supermarket chain said its revamped Asda Rewards programme helped attract online customers. Rivals Tesco, with its Clubcard, and Sainsbury’s Nectar programme have seen a significant uptick in users in recent years.

Asda said it would focus on offering customers value for money at a time UK household budgets are under pressure from higher prices and mortgage costs.

The latest Asda Income Tracker, a measure of affordability, showed spending power at a six-month low and the lowest-earning households facing an average £76 (RM410.65) shortfall on essential bills.

See also: UK PM's rejection of EU financial rules shows Brexit reset limit

Intense competition in the grocery industry has led to recent speculation about consolidation. Asda was the target of a takeover bid by Sainsbury’s that was blocked by regulators in 2019 over concerns it would lead to higher prices and reduced competition.

title: Billionaire KoGuan vows to stop buying Nvidia after Huang exit
article:
(Nov 13): Billionaire investor and Nvidia Corp shareholder Leo KoGuan expressed support for Jensen Huang on Friday and said he won’t increase his stake in the tech company with someone else at the helm.

“No further investment without Jensen,” KoGuan said in a text message, saying he’s invested around US$1.3 billion in Nvidia.

In a series of posts on X, KoGuan called Huang “the supreme creator” and acknowledged that while the executive had made errors, “we must prioritise rewards” rather “than punishments”.

The posts followed Huang’s abrupt ouster from Nvidia after reports of three affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. That ended his decades-long reign over a company at the center of the artificial intelligence buildout and, by extension, the global economy.

Singapore-based KoGuan, who has a US$13.2 billion fortune, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, began investing in Nvidia in March. It was a notable move for an investor whose net worth for years had been tied up largely in one stock: Tesla Inc. The size of KoGuan’s Nvidia stake couldn’t be independently verified.

Earlier this week, KoGuan said on X that he’s also an investor in Space Exploration Technologies Corp and Google, whose parent is Alphabet Inc. He told Bloomberg that he plans on increasing his positions in those companies.

See also: Microsoft races to fix Outlook in one of its longest outages

Investors must buy and hold super-intelligence companies for the long term, he wrote on X.

“I hope and plan to invest in Jensen Huang if he creates or buys” another super-intelligence company, he wrote on Friday. “I hope he will offer me the opportunity to invest in his future company.”

title: US wholesale inflation picks up to fastest pace since 2022
article:
(Nov 13): US wholesale inflation climbed in October from a year earlier at the fastest pace since 2022, adding to evidence of mounting price pressures throughout the economy.

The producer price index rose 6.5% from October 2025, an acceleration from the prior month, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data out on Friday. On a monthly basis, the PPI increased 0.3%.

Excluding food and energy, wholesale prices climbed 5% from a year ago and 0.3% from September.

The annual increase in the PPI illustrates how a supply-related surge this year in energy prices as well as robust demand are fanning inflationary pressures. The report showed another jump in transportation and warehousing costs, as well as higher food prices.

Figures earlier this week showed a gauge of underlying consumer inflation posted another firm advance during the month. Some Federal Reserve officials have signalled they may need to more aggressive with policy to bring down inflation.

See also: Existing US home sales tumble to lowest level since 2010

Fed officials are widely expected to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point at the conclusion of their two-day meeting on Dec 9.

title: Hongkong Land's pace of capital recycling ahead of target after selling another US$500 mil worth
article:
Hongkong Land Holdings says its capital recycling move is tracking ahead of schedule, with some US$4.2 billion worth of assets recycled, versus the original stated target of at least US$4 billion by end of 2027.

This broad direction, in turn, is part of a US$10 billion recycling target by 2035, first laid down in October 2024.

Proceeds from the divestments, according to Hongkong Land, will be used to fund growth in its "ultra-premium" commercial property portfolios and enhance shareholder returns, with a greater proportion to be realised in the short to medium term.

In the last couple of years, Hongkong Land is known for monetising assets including certain floors of commercial properties in Hong Kong.

What the company has just announced, is that thus far this year, it has sold "selected interests" in its properties in southeast Asia worth US$500 million.

Hongkong Land says its primary strategy is to simplify its prime properties investment portfolio and focus on its anchor markets of Hong Kong, Singapore and the Chinese Mainland.

See also: Schroders said to seek mall sale in bid to offload Singapore properties

These transactions cover investments across Cambodia, the Philippines and Thailand, namely, the disposal of its 49% interest in the development of the former British Embassy site in Bangkok.

Each of the above transactions, pending applicable regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, was concluded at market value and at, or above, the company’s carrying value.

On the other hand, Hongkong Land has been using some of the proceeds from the divestments to buy back shares.

See also: Besides healthcare top pick, Nuveen Real Estate touts grocery-anchored retail in many markets

The company is adding another US$100 million to the buy back programme also announced in Oct 2024 to US$750 million. To date, some US$508.5 million worth of shares has been bought back.

The share buyback programme period will also be extended through to Dec 31 2027, from June 30 2027.

"The pace at which the programme is executed will remain discretionary and subject to market conditions," the company says.

"This progress reflects our deliberate efforts to sharpen our portfolio focus, streamline our geographic footprint and concentrate capital and resources where we see the greatest opportunities to create long term value," says group CEO Michael T Smith.

"We have further strengthened our balance sheet, providing greater flexibility to invest in our core portfolios and pursue disciplined growth in Asian gateway cities.

"Importantly, these transactions also enable us to increase and extend our share buyback programme, underscoring our commitment to disciplined capital allocation and delivering long-term value for shareholders," he adds.

title: Investors warn bond rout not over after week of soaring yields
article:
(Nov 13): Just when global bond investors were starting to believe the worst of this year’s rout was over, surging Treasury yields are making them think again.

The forces roiling the world’s biggest debt market show little sign of fading, as stubborn inflation and hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric have traders bracing for more interest-rate hikes, while growing debt supply adds to the upward pressure on yields. The selloff persisted even as turmoil around Nvidia Corp rattled stocks and risk sentiment, undercutting hopes that Treasuries had reclaimed their traditional haven role.

“This is a tougher environment than during the Covid pandemic and the global financial crisis,” said Kellie Wood, a Sydney-based money manager at Schroders Plc who is currently short Treasuries. “Those were big directional moves — today it’s about rolling supply shocks and wild rates volatility. We still have to be on alert for higher yields all the way till year-end.”

Treasuries have had a bruising week, with the selloff stretching beyond the policy-sensitive front end. The combined jump in two-year US yields on Tuesday and Thursday — with cash markets closed on Wednesday — was the biggest since March 2023, while the increase in 10-year yields was the most since April 2025. By Friday, the two-year yield was at 4.85% and the 10-year at 5.12%, both close to the highest in one month.

It’s a U-turn from just a week ago, when a Democratic sweep in the US midterms and jitters over artificial intelligence (AI) sent investors flocking to Treasuries for safety. That rush of bullish positioning has since been upended, after Fed governor Christopher Waller backed a rate increase and said he’d favour a half-point hike if inflation keeps accelerating. A hotter-than-expected consumer price report reinforced the shift, as did comments from Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan.

See also: South Korea fines bond dealers record US$1.2 bil over collusion

The pressure is rippling through global markets, with Treasuries setting the benchmark for borrowing costs worldwide. A Bloomberg gauge of returns on Treasuries is sliding again after the latest surge in yields, reversing a recovery that had pared its loss this year to 1%.

“The selloff of developed-market sovereign bonds is far from over,” said Tracy Chen, a portfolio manager at Brandywine Global Investment Management, adding that the main drivers are still going strong. “The next target level for 10-year should head toward 5.5% and then probably consolidate again.”

“The selloff in two-year Treasuries has room to extend when the next leg of inflation data is released on Friday,” says Alyce Andres, Markets Live strategist at Bloomberg Strategists.

See also: US Treasuries stumble as strong jobs data backs Fed-hike bets

For some investors, the rise in yields is creating an opportunity. George Boubouras at hedge fund K2 Asset Management sees 10-year Treasuries as attractive at around 5.3%, saying the recent rally wasn’t a false start.

“We’re buyers of it at 5.3%, and we’ll be buyers of that until it pops to the new level,” said Boubouras, its managing director and head of research, investments and advisory, in Melbourne.

Strategists at Goldman Sachs Group Inc this week forecast US 10-year yields will drop to 4.6% in 2027, citing the rising appeal of hedging and benign inflation.

Beyond the US, yields in Japan and Australia are climbing back towards multiyear highs. Those in France, which have surged on concern over the nation’s fiscal outlook and political instability, are also resuming their advance after easing earlier in November.

Traders are ramping up bets on tighter policy globally. Swaps are pricing in an average change of more than 50 basis points (bps) in policy rates over the coming year across eight economies, up from 33bps seen on Nov 6, which was the lowest since June, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“Barring an abject crash in risk assets like stocks, or a return of oil prices to pre-war levels, the risk is that the banks will have to go further than the market is currently assuming,” Steven Barrow, head of G10 strategy at Standard Bank Group in London, wrote in a note.

Schroders’ Wood sees a more divided picture. While US rates may need to rise — potentially over 5% — as inflation accelerates and growth outpaces the rest of the world, she is long bonds in Australia and Europe, betting central banks there will ease in 2027 to head off recession.

“2027 will be the year of dispersion with each economy at a different stage of the cycle,” she said. “2027 is the year for the active bond manager.”

title: Bitcoin slides below US$70,000 as inflation concerns hurt crypto
article:
(Nov 13): Bitcoin fell below US$70,000 on Friday for the first time since August, extending a two-day slump to as much as 9% as concerns about inflation and higher interest rates weighed on cryptocurrencies.

The largest digital asset sank as much as 5.4% to US$67,628, its lowest level since Aug 19, adding to a 3.8% decline on Thursday. It later pared some losses to trade around US$69,200 in early morning in New York.

Roughly US$1.5 billion in bullish bets on cryptocurrencies were liquidated over a 24-hour period, according to CoinGlass data. Forced selling by leveraged traders added momentum to the decline.

“Once it broke below US$70,000, over US$1 billion of leveraged longs were forced out, which fed more selling,” said Sean McNulty, a derivatives trader at market maker AQC Tech. Ether, the second-largest token, fell as much as 6%, bringing it back under US$2,000.

Bitcoin’s weakness reflects a convergence of macro pressures on crypto in recent weeks. Elevated oil prices and persistent inflation have reinforced expectations for additional Federal Reserve rate increases. Democrats retaking both chambers of the US Congress next year following the midterm elections has raised expectations of greater regulatory scrutiny on the industry.

See also: Thailand lets tourists turn crypto into baht for spending

This week, a key gauge of US consumer prices posted another firm advance in October, keeping the Fed on track to raise rates next month. The consumer price index, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% from a month earlier, topping estimates for a third straight month. Overall prices jumped 0.4% as the cost of essentials climbed across the board.

“If the Fed hikes rates by 50 basis points (bps) rather than the expected 25bps, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies could have more room to fall,” said Jeff Mei, chief operating officer of crypto exchange BTSE,

See also: Bitcoin retreats as Nvidia turmoil weighs on risk appetite

US stocks were subdued ahead of inflation data, capping a volatile week marked by rising bets on Fed rate hikes and Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia Corp. S&P 500 futures edged 0.1% higher while Nasdaq 100 contracts were flat.

Rich Rosenblum, co-founder of crypto market maker GSR, said volatility in the artificial intelligence trade and continued US dollar strength have washed out some long Bitcoin positions, while the hot inflation data and changes in Nvidia’s leadership are also dragging on risk assets.

Institutional buyers have also been on the retreat for the past two weeks. Since Oct 30, US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have seen more than US$2.5 billion in net outflows.

title: Microsoft races to fix Outlook in one of its longest outages
article:
(Nov 13): Microsoft Corp is struggling to restore access to its flagship software and end an outage that has paralysed government offices, traders and businesses globally.

Disruptions for Outlook, Teams and the Copilot artificial intelligence tool continued into a second day on Friday as Microsoft struggled to restore services. Previous disruptions have rarely lasted more than several hours.

The company has provided near hourly updates of its efforts to fix its malfunctioning systems and route user traffic away from affected servers. It said an investigation into the incident had found “a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss”, and said the cause wasn’t obviously malicious. Microsoft said in a status update on Friday that it was seeing “positive signs for server stability”, though services have not been restored.

Companies relying on Microsoft systems, including Swiss luxury group Richemont SA and US-based truck and bus manufacturer Workhorse Group Inc, had to postpone earnings releases this week. Richemont has since filed its report.

PVH Corp, the apparel conglomerate that owns the Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger brands, announced Thursday in internal company emails and stock exchange filings that it would cut about 4% of its global workforce. Some of the difficult conversations, scheduled to start in Asia on Friday morning, did not take place because of the outages, leaving employees uncertain of their future at the company, according to a person familiar with the matter, who requested anonymity to describe private matters. PVH did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The outage shows the ubiquity of Microsoft’s email, chat and corporate software and is another example of the risks of having a single point of failure on the internet. While most technology glitches are fixed quickly, faulty updates and server troubles at one key technology provider can ripple across the global economy. A 15-hour disruption at Amazon Web Services last year hit hundreds of websites. A faulty software update from cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike Holdings Inc in 2024 grounded flights and crashed systems around the world, causing billions of dollars in damages.

See also: Singapore charges fifth person as Nvidia case expands

Users in more than 70 countries reported problems accessing Microsoft’s products, according to Downdetector, which recorded hundreds of thousands of complaints. Cybersecurity software, file-sharing services and administrator tools, were also disrupted. The company sells those products, along with workplace staples like Word and Excel, in a bundle under the M365 brand.

In the UK, Guy’s and St Thomas’ warned patients that email was offline, though the London hospital’s procedures were going ahead as planned. A number of local police forces also said they couldn’t take crime reports online, according to the Guardian newspaper.

Traders in Singapore, Indian brokerages and officials in Tokyo also reported issues with Microsoft services on Friday. Euronext sent a warning that its email communications were unavailable.

See also: The tech brotherhood wants sovereignty

Japan’s finance ministry said in a statement that it had been unable to receive emails for most of the day. Without access to their email, government ministries resorted to pinning up paper notices to inform journalists about daily schedules.

Staffers at the Reserve Bank of Australia were also impacted, with Outlook down across departments at the bank, but critical operations ran normally. In New Zealand, immigration officials paused the processing of all visa applications.

title: China not bidding to host 2028 UN climate talks — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): China has decided against bidding to host the United Nations climate summit in 2028, an event that is scheduled to coincide with the next US presidential election.

Officials deliberated over a proposal and have now opted not to proceed, according to people familiar with the situation, who requested anonymity to discuss private discussions.

The people didn’t cite any reason for China’s conclusion, though the event would fall two years ahead of the country’s deadline to peak its carbon dioxide emissions.

Talks on the issue in recent months involved the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and environmental officials, and a final endorsement had required support from the highest levels of government, Bloomberg News reported in August. The Guardian first reported news that China would not formally bid to act as host.

China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said she did not have information to share on the issue at a regular press briefing on Friday. The COP process “is an important platform for global climate governance,” she said. “China is committed to advancing global green and low carbon transition and international cooperation on climate response.”

See also: Türkiye finance chief says climate goals need US$300 bil

The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the organisation that convenes COP meetings between almost 200 countries, also didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Negotiations are currently taking place at the COP31 conference in Antalya, Turkey, and will be hosted by Ethiopia in Addis Ababa in 2027. Duties are rotated between regional blocs with the Asia-Pacific states, a group of more than 50 countries which also includes Japan, South Korea and Indonesia, due to provide a venue in 2028. A decision doesn’t need to be taken at the current talks in Antalya, and could come at next year’s summit.

South Korea hasn’t expressed any intention to host, and will already stage G20 events in 2028, a climate, energy and environment ministry spokesperson said. “Our position appears to be that it would likely be difficult,” the spokesperson said.

See also: EU climate chief rules out fresh finance pledges at COP31

Indonesia and Uzbekistan have signalled their potential interest to host, according to a person familiar with the matter. However, no country has yet submitted a new official bid to the Asia-Pacific group after India in April withdrew an offer to host the negotiations.

Representatives for Indonesia and Uzbekistan didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

Climate advocates had seen a potential China-hosted COP as an opportunity to inject fresh momentum into the waning campaign to tackle global warming by sending a definitive signal about the intentions of the world’s current largest emitter.

The 2028 talks are also a significant negotiating event and scheduled to complete an assessment of progress towards Paris Agreement goals that will help steer the pace and scope of future international action.

Agreeing to stage a COP summit can add pressure on host nations and is a complex decision for China, said Patricia Espinosa, former executive secretary of the UNFCCC. “You get to be in the centre of attention of everybody, you also have a big expectations internally, so it has become quite complicated,” she said. “You know that you will be exposed to to criticism.”

China has signalled this year that it aims to take a more important role in steering global climate diplomacy, and pledged to “constructively lead the multilateral governance process,” in a latest five-year plan published in July by the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, the National Development and Reform Commission, and other key agencies.

Nations should “deepen international cooperation,” Vice President Han Zheng told a meeting of world leaders at the Antalya talks on Wednesday. “It is important to offer more support and assistance to developing countries.”

title: Q&M Dental completes THB 994.5 mil acquisition of 51% stake in Thai dental group
article:
Q & M Dental Group (Singapore) has completed the THB994.5 million ($37.76 million) acquisition of a 51% stake in Deezy Q & M Dental Group (Thailand), which owns and operates the Deezy Dental Home network of 33 dental clinics across Bangkok and north-eastern Thailand.

The acquisition marks Q&M’s entry into Thailand and extends its dental network beyond Singapore, Malaysia and China.

The acquisition, first announced on July 10, is to be paid with THB 700 million in cash, funded partly by bank borrowings and partly by internal resources, and another THB 294.5 million in 16,375,714 new shares issued at 70 cents each.

Deezy was founded in 2017 by Dr Nanthisak Piyanantisak and Dr Thunyaporn Pongkajornkitjakarn.

Since then, it has grown to become one of Thailand’s established private dental networks manned by 411 dentists, serving more than 400,000 patients.

Under terms of the deal, the sellers have provided a profit guarantee of around THB 1.25 billion in Deezy’s net profit for the six years from Nov 1 2026 to Oct 31 2032.

See also: Samsung in talks to acquire data centre cooling firm Modine — Bloomberg

Any shortfall is to be made good first through the sellers waiving their dividend entitlements in the company’s favour.

Any remaining shortfall is to be met by the guarantors, Dr Nanthisak and Dr Thunyaporn, with 70.4% from an escrow account and 29.6% through the sale of the consideration shares, which are to be pledged to the company as security.

Where either source falls short, the guarantors are to pay the balance in cash within 90 days of the financial statements for the relevant period being determined.

See also: Unilever-McCormick deal facing in-depth review from UK watchdog

If a shortfall is not settled within 90 days, the company may require the vendor and the guarantors to buy back the shares it

acquired under the SPA, at the full consideration plus a simple return of 10% per annum from completion.

Dr Thunyaporn and Dr Nanthisak will remain with Deezy as a key dentist and in a management role respectively, under 15-year service agreements that include non-compete and non-solicitation terms.

Q&M says this deal gives it an immediate foothold in Thailand’s private dental market without the need to build operations from the ground up, and a platform that can be expanded through organic growth and future acquisitions.

"Our focus now is on integration. We intend to preserve what has made Deezy successful in its home market, while bringing the group’s experience in clinical governance, procurement and dentist training to support its growth in the years ahead," says Dr Ng Chin Siau, group CEO of Q & M Dental Group (Singapore).

"By combining Deezy’s local expertise with Q & M’s technology and regional experience, we can reach more communities while strengthening collaboration, knowledge sharing and professional development between dentists in Thailand and Singapore," says Dr Nanthisak Piyanantisak.

Q&M Dental shares closed at 48 cents on Nov 13, down 1.04% for the day, extending a drop of 13.64% year to date.

title: Post-Jensen US chip curbs threaten Southeast Asia’s AI boom
article:
(Nov 13): Southeast Asia risks facing tighter US regulations on the export and use of high-powered chips, threatening to stall the region’s AI-fuelled economic boom.

The fallout from Nvidia Corp chief Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy working at a firm with ties to Singapore and Malaysia has increased scrutiny of the shipment and use of US-restricted chips in Southeast Asia.

Some in the Trump administration fear that places such as Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand have been weak points in global efforts to keep the most advanced tech from China — either as transit points for the diversion of the chips or as hosts to data centres with restricted chips that are used remotely by Chinese firms.

While Huang’s exit removes one of the most high-profile proponents against stringent restrictions in Washington, the scale of the expected tightening is still unclear.

Legislation that may pass by the end of the year could include firmer restrictions on the sale of high-end chips to foreign countries. As well, the US Commerce Department is looking at imposing new export rules and licensing requirements to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Governments are already seeking to assuage the security concerns. Singapore charged a fifth person on Friday in relation to an AI server fraud case, while Malaysia is investigating whether AI chips brought into the country have been subsequently shipped overseas.

See also: Why compute will be the next big AI trade

“This would put a dampener on the demand for AI compute in existing and future data centres in Southeast Asia,” said Malaysia’s former deputy trade minister Ong Kian Ming, adding that new laws further restricting access and use would be hard to mitigate and manage for governments in the region.

“Malaysia would take the brunt of the likely drop in demand but this may also have spillover effects to Thailand and Indonesia,” he said. “Singapore also may not be spared if this limits the ability of some of the AI players” registered in the city-state.

Data centres have emerged as an unexpected growth driver for Southeast Asia this year, alongside the boost from semiconductor and related AI exports, offsetting the drag from higher oil prices and interest rates.

See also: ByteDance said to prepare Muse-like agent in push to close AI gap

Chinese demand for computing capacity in Southeast Asia could be reduced, introducing greater risk to the data centre investment pipeline, according to Brian Lee, an analyst for Maybank Securities Pte Ltd.

Malaysia and Thailand have been hotspots for data centre investments, while Indonesia’s data centre market is in earlier stages of development, Lee said.

“Data centre investment demand is nonetheless also driven by domestic cloud demand, digital services and the broader digital economy, which may not require the advanced Blackwell class Nvidia GPUs under proposed export controls,” he added.

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was likewise sanguine, saying Friday that US and Chinese firms alike have reaffirmed their commitment to invest in the country. Senior Indonesian minister Airlangga Hartarto said his country has been in talks with Washington about a US-led effort to secure global AI and semiconductor supply chains.

Southeast Asia’s appeal is hinged on its attractive power, land and regulatory environment for hyperscalers, according to a September report by Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

“Another driver is export-control arbitrage, as Chinese players can use Asean as a platform for deploying US chips in model training for non-China markets,” it said.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

It’s unclear exactly how much of Southeast Asia’s computing resources have been tapped by Chinese firms, as buyers of Nvidia chips have been reluctant to disclose the identities of their clients. But within the industry the demand is seen as a major driver of the region’s data centre boom.

Goldman forecasts Southeast Asia’s data centre capacity would grow fourfold in the next five years, with the Malaysian state of Johor to be the largest hub in Asean by 2030. It estimates Malaysia should see an average growth boost of 30 basis points from 2026 to 2028, while Thailand gets an additional 20 basis points.

Cameron Systermans, who heads Asia multi-asset for consultancy Marsh, said the region may see “more selectivity, rather than a broad retreat” in light of the Nvidia fallout.

The fundamental drivers of the region’s data centre build out remain strong, as AI adoption and cloud use expand rapidly, he said. Southeast Asia is a strategic location for investors seeking to diversify supply chains and build digital capacity closer to fast-growing markets.

“The most attractive markets and projects will be those that can combine growth potential with reliable infrastructure, transparent investment structures, and a stable regulatory environment,” he said. “Capital will become more discerning.”

title: Singapore charges fifth person as Nvidia case expands
article:
(Nov 13): Singapore charged a fifth person in a fraud case linked to the export of computer hardware suspected of containing Nvidia Corp chips subject to US trade restrictions.

Shi Bingzhe, 34, was handed 41 charges including for money laundering offences on Friday, the Singapore police said in a statement. Singapore Police Force also handed separate charges to Superphi Pte Ltd and NJ Global Financial Pte Ltd, two companies where Shi worked as a director.

Authorities in Singapore and elsewhere in Southeast Asia are stepping up their scrutiny of shipments of advanced Nvidia AI chips that the US suspects are being smuggled to China via the region. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive officer on Thursday after revelations that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, a former CEO of a Singapore-based firm also suspected of helping Chinese companies procure Nvidia chips.

With Shi’s consent, Singaporean firms Superphi and NJ Global acquired a total of 917 servers from Aperia International Pte Ltd across 41 transactions between May 2024 and February 2025, the police said. The firms had reasonable grounds to believe that those servers represented benefits from Aperia International’s criminal conduct including fraud by false representation, the police said.

If convicted, Shi faces up to 10 years in jail for each case, or a fine of up to $500,000, or both. Superphi and NJ Global face a fine of up to $1 million or twice the value of the benefits from criminal conduct, whichever is higher, for each charge, the police said.

Four companies connected to the case were charged in July with fraud by false representation: Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech Pte Ltd, Aperia Cloud Services (II) Pte Ltd and Luxuriate Your Life Pte Ltd. Singapore police said then the case involved alleged false statements about the end-users of servers bought from Dell Technologies Inc, Super Micro Computer Inc and Asustek Computer Inc.

See also: The tech brotherhood wants sovereignty

Apart from Shi, Singapore has charged four others with related offences including fraud, money laundering and fraudulent trading. Prosecutors said in March 2025 that the alleged transactions totalled about US$390 million ($502 million).

The case has put Singapore and neighbouring Malaysia under scrutiny over whether advanced AI hardware subject to US export curbs was being routed through the region. Singapore launched an independent investigation after an anonymous tip and has said it is examining potential breaches of domestic law. Malaysia separately investigated whether local laws were breached by the server shipments.

Singapore said last year that the servers were shipped onwards to Malaysia and may have contained Nvidia chips. Authorities have been trying to determine whether Malaysia was the final destination in the case, which has highlighted the role of middlemen in funnelling high-end semiconductors.

title: IOIPG REIT lowers IPO price to 91 sen, public tranche oversubscribed 0.59 times
article:
IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG REIT) has trimmed its initial public offering (IPO) price to 91 sen for both retail and institutional investors.

The IPO price revision from 96 sen per share followed bookbuilding for the institutional offering, according to a statement issued by Malaysian Issuing House Sdn Bhd on Nov 12.

It will refund five sen to successful applicants under the retail offering.

“Against a backdrop of market uncertainties, the institutional offering successfully secured interest predominantly from notable long-only investors, including government-linked investment companies and insurers,” the statement read.

“The participation of these long-only institutions reflects their confidence in the quality of IOIPG REIT’s portfolio and its access to IOIPG’s robust pipeline of assets.

“In determining the institutional price, the IOIPG REIT Management Sdn Bhd and IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) also recognised the level of support shown by IOI Properties Group shareholders through their participation in the restricted offering. The institutional price also offers IOI Properties Group’s shareholders the opportunity to invest in IOIPG REIT at the pro forma net asset value of IOIPG REIT and participate in the long-term growth of IOIPG REIT,” it added.

See also: Anthropic’s IPO is about six times oversubscribed — Bloomberg

The revised IPO price values IOIPG REIT at RM5 billion, down from RM5.3 billion.

Successful applicants will be notified of their allotments by Nov 24. IOIPG REIT is slated to list on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia on Nov 25.

Meanwhile, its IPO was oversubscribed by 0.59 times under the Malaysian public portion. The public tranche, comprising 110 million offer units, received 10,859 applications for 175 million units.

See also: Carlsberg said set to start road show for US$600 mil India IPO — Bloomberg

The Bumiputera portion, comprising 55 million units, was undersubscribed. The tranche's subscription rate stood 0.33 times — 1,745 applications for 18.24 million units. The balance was clawed back and reallocated.

The other Malaysian public portion, comprising the same number of units, received 9,114 applications for 156.76 million units, representing an oversubscription rate of 1.85 times.

For the restricted offering to shareholders of IOI Properties Group, comprising 550.61 million units, it received valid acceptances for 604.18 million units, representing an oversubscription rate of 1.1 times.

Units under the restricted pink form offering to eligible directors, employees and business associates, comprising 55 million units, were fully subscribed. The institutional offering, comprising up to 1.48 billion units, was also fully subscribed.

Maybank Investment Bank Bhd and AmInvestment Bank Bhd are the joint principal advisers, joint global coordinators, joint bookrunners, joint managing underwriters and joint underwriters for the IPO.

DBS Bank Ltd is a joint global coordinator and joint bookrunner.

CIMB Investment Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd, RHB Investment Bank Bhd and UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd are the joint bookrunners and joint underwriters. Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Ltd is also a joint bookrunner.

title: Oil-hungry Asia turns back to Mideast in earnest as flows expand
article:
(Nov 13): Oil refiners in Asia are increasingly turning back towards crude from Middle Eastern producers as flows rebound after months of conflict, lessening the need for imports from alternative suppliers including the US.

Refiners in countries including Japan, China and Thailand have either ramped up or restarted buying from the region, including supplies that need to cross the still-contested Strait of Hormuz, according to traders familiar with the matter, asking not to be named discussing commercial matters. Greater volumes are coming from the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar, they said.

The global oil market is showing increasing signs of reverting to patterns seen before the outbreak of war between the US and Iran in February, even as the sides have yet to reach a resolution. Among them is a sustained preference from refiners in the world’s biggest importing region to rely on the Middle East for cargoes. Slumping prices and weaker freight rates add to the picture.

“How do you break the reliance on your biggest source of crude? There is just not enough slack in global balances to move the needle significantly when it comes to trying to diversify,” said Warren Patterson, head of commodities strategy for ING Groep NV, referring to Asia’s appetite for Mideast oil.

In the early stages of the war, flows from Persian Gulf shippers sank as tankers passing through Hormuz were targeted, along with energy infrastructure. Output has since rebounded, with Saudi Arabia telling Opec its oil output surged in October to one of the highest monthly levels in years. That means less demand from Asian buyers for stopgaps, including from the distant US.

See also: BP in talks to sell stake in Brazil oil discovery to Petrobras — Bloomberg

At the same time, major Middle Eastern producers have slashed term rates for Asian buyers, as they compete more aggressively for market share. Saudi Arabia recently cut official selling prices to the region to a fresh six-year low, while the United Arab Emirates — which quit the OPEC cartel in April — has reduced the price premium for December supplies of its flagship grade.

Asian refinery orders for US crude for delivery in November tumbled roughly 50% to 24 million to 26 million barrels, traders told Bloomberg last month. Separately, Port of Corpus Christi chief executive officer Kent Britton — head of the US largest port — said this week that none of the 40 crude cargoes that departed US Gulf Coast ports last week was bound for Asia.

See also: Rising fuel flows through Hormuz may help ease strained market

While shipping costs have slid across the board in recent weeks, those for US-to-Asia voyages have softened more than other routes, showing the revived preference from Asian refiners for Middle Eastern oil. Daily earnings for very large crude carriers on routes from the US Gulf are down 61% from an October peak, compared with just 24% from the Persian Gulf to East Asia.

In China — the world’s largest oil buyer — nationwide crude imports rose to a seven-month high in October, marked by a recovery in shipments from the Persian Gulf. The purchases climbed to nearly 42 million tons, led by Iraqi cargoes, according to official customs data this week.

In Japan, refiners including Eneos Holdings Inc. and Cosmo Energy Holdings Co had been among recent purchasers of oil from the UAE, traders said. Meanwhile, independent Chinese processors have been ordering more prompt supplies from Iraq, they said. India’s imports from the Persian Gulf, meanwhile, have now topped volumes from Russia, according to Kpler data.

For Japanese importers, as long as they “can still get crude from the Middle East, refiners will probably keep buying it,” said Yutaro Nishi, an analyst at the Rakuten Securities Economic Research Institute.

“It varies from country to country, but I don’t think the basic picture is going to change,” the former commodities trader added. “Asia will remain a major market for Middle Eastern crude.”

title: ByteDance plans US$6 bil buyback at US$400 bil valuation — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): ByteDance Ltd plans to buy back up to US$6 billion of shares from investors at a valuation of about US$400 billion, marking a 20% uptick from a similar programme a year ago, according to people who’ve reviewed the proposal.

TikTok’s Chinese owner informed investors of the offer in a recent letter, setting the price at US$241.35 per share, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private information. ByteDance is also proposing to push out by four years its deadline to either go public or grant external shareholders the right to sell back their entire stakes, to Dec 11, 2030, one of the people said.

A ByteDance spokesperson didn’t respond to requests for comment on the initiatives, which were first reported by The Information.

In its letter to shareholders, ByteDance also detailed plans to offer employees at its artificial intelligence division a total of 300 million shares that track the value of its AI business, one of the people said. The move comes as the company ramps up enticements to recruit and retain AI talent. It’s already offering preferential equity arrangements that set those staffers apart from the rest of the company.

Beijing-based ByteDance became the world’s most valuable startup after pioneering algorithmic recommendations in TikTok and its Chinese twin Douyin, yet fell behind in the ChatGPT era. After top brass urged staff in 2024 to redouble efforts, it gained traction in AI with its Doubao chatbot, now China’s most popular, and its Seedance video-generation service.

To catch up on large language models, billionaire co-founder Zhang Yiming recently rallied the AI team around a goal of competing with industry-leading US labs within the next three years, Bloomberg News has reported. The company also plans to launch a sophisticated personal AI assistant to serve similar functions to Muse by Meta Platforms Inc.

See also: Advent again seeks to sell Singapore tutor-chain Learning Lab — Bloomberg

It’s unclear when ByteDance or any individual parts of its business could debut on public markets. Some existing investors have valued the company at above $400 billion, and its value has approached $500 billion in some secondary transactions.

title: Anthropic’s IPO is about six times oversubscribed — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering (IPO) has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter, as interest increases for potentially the biggest first-time share sale ever.

The Claude AI model firm and its co-founders are seeking to raise as much as US$64.4 billion ($82.9 billion) in the IPO and US$26 billion in a private placement, its filings show. Taken together, the offering would be bigger than SpaceX’s IPO, making it the biggest listing of all time.

Bankers have told prospective investors that existing backers will be prioritised by Anthropic, and some would-be buyers will receive smaller allocations than they expect, some of the people said.

Details of the IPO including the demand for shares could change, said the people, who asked not to be identified as the information isn’t public. A representative for Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The surge of interest in Anthropic shares contrasts with investors pulling back support for Nvidia Corp after chief executive officer Jensen Huang was ousted from his post after reports of several affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China.

The chipmaker has agreed to buy about US$10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic as part of a US$26 billion private placement concurrent with its IPO, the AI model firm’s filings show. Anthropic counts Nvidia as a strategic partner, and has committed tens of billions of dollars to deals securing access to its most advanced chips.

See also: Carlsberg said set to start road show for US$600 mil India IPO — Bloomberg

Anthropic is looking to bolster demand for the IPO with a campaign of events for prospective investors, including a live-streamed event with its chief executive officer Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, a person familiar with the matter has said.

The company is targeting a fully diluted valuation of about US$1.4 trillion, below where some investors expected the company to settle, Bloomberg News reported. Some companies set terms conservatively when they begin formally marketing their IPO, in the expectation that strong demand will push up the final figure and set them up for robust trading in their debuts.

Anthropic’s filing Tuesday supported the case for AI spending as sales continued to increase. The company reported a revenue run rate of US$81 billion as of Oct 31, up US$10 billion from the end of September, the filing showed. Anthropic had a US$65 billion run rate figure at the end of July, Bloomberg News reported. Anthropic defines the metric as annualizing consumption-based fees for a trailing 28-day period and subscription-based fees for a single month.

See also: Bankers looking at raising Anthropic's valuation to US$1.5 tril or more — FT

Some investors are offering a portion of their Anthropic IPO allocation to other prospective backers, letting them collect additional fees and reduce their risk before trading begins, while others with pre-IPO stakes are marketing them to buyers via special purpose vehicles.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley are leading Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing shows. The stock is expected to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.

title: Advent again seeks to sell Singapore tutor-chain Learning Lab — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): US buyout firm Advent International Corp has put up Singapore’s tutor-chain The Learning Lab for sale, marking its second attempt since 2021 to unload the asset, in part to repay debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

Advent has hired an advisor to kickstart the sale process and plans to offer the company for about US$400 million ($515 million) to US$500 million, said the people who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. Some of the proceeds will be used to settle a $265 million private credit facility jointly provided by KKR & Co Inc, HPS Investment Partners and Nomura Holdings Inc in 2023 and which will mature next year, they said.

Representatives for Advent, KKR and Nomura declined to comment. HPS didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Private money has been pouring into schools in Asia in recent years as investors seek to profit from growing demand for quality education. Financiers such as Apollo Global Management Inc and KKR & Co Inc have bought stakes and lent to school chains, hoping that a growing number of rich people in the region would fuel expansion.

But private equity and venture capital investment in education services in Asia slumped 87% to US$240 million last year, according to S&P Global, citing more rigorous deal selection and the potential impact of artificial intelligence on the sector. Another key challenge is the backlog of private equity firms seeking to exit companies they’ve bought into.

Advent invested in The Learning Lab in 2014, but there has been no publicly available information on how much stake it holds. People with knowledge of the matter said Advent fully owns the learning company.

See also: US probes if Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products — Bloomberg

The Learning Lab provides education for preschool, primary, secondary and junior college students in Singapore, according to its website. It also has online services for other Asian markets including Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia. In Singapore, the company charges about $702 a month for its junior college programmes.

title: Thailand lets tourists turn crypto into baht for spending
article:
(Nov 13): A new payment app in Thailand is looking to tap tourists’ crypto wealth as the country struggles to revive tourism spending.

WORPT lets foreign visitors convert cryptocurrency into baht and spend it at shops and restaurants by scanning barcodes widely used for payments in the country, without needing a Thai bank account.

The app was developed by Wipay Co and Waan Exchange Co, founded by Chaval Jiaravanon of Thailand’s billionaire Chearavanont family. It operates under TouristDigiPay, a regulatory pilot launched by Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission.

Similar crypto-funded payment services for foreign visitors were introduced in Bhutan and Brazil in 2025.

The rollout comes as Thailand’s foreign arrivals head for a second straight annual decline and international tourism revenue also falls. Tourism is a major driver of the economy, and the government is increasingly focused on attracting higher-spending visitors.

WORPT is targeting crypto holders from South Korea, Japan, the Middle East and Southeast Asia, according to Wipay founder Pavin Jittiwongsamarn. The company expects 200,000 users in its first year and projects 15 billion baht (US$440 million) of spending over the 18-month trial.

See also: Bitcoin retreats as Nvidia turmoil weighs on risk appetite

title: Carlsberg said set to start road show for US$600 mil India IPO — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): Carlsberg A/S is set to start investor meetings as early as next week for an initial public offering (IPO) of its India business that could raise as much as US$600 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

Carlsberg India Ltd, the country’s second-largest brewer, could launch the IPO as early as January, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The Danish brewer is seeking a valuation of US$4 billion for the India business, the people said.

Deliberations are ongoing and details including the size, structure and timing of the transaction could still change, the people said. A representative for Carlsberg declined to comment.

The proposed offering would consist entirely of a secondary share sale by the Danish parent. Carlsberg entity South Asian Breweries Pte Ltd plans to sell as many as 86.42 million shares, representing 15% of the company’s equity capital, according to the prospectus. Carlsberg confidentially submitted draft IPO documents in July and made its filing public on Oct 27.

Carlsberg has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital Co, Citigroup Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co to manage the offering, the prospectus shows.

Strong demand for Jio Platforms Ltd’s record US$3.1 billion IPO and its post-listing performance have boosted confidence among prospective issuers looking to press ahead with large transactions. Investors’ ability to absorb such offerings could encourage more companies waiting on the sidelines to accelerate their listing plans, potentially keeping India among the world’s busiest markets for new share sales into 2027.

See also: Bankers looking at raising Anthropic's valuation to US$1.5 tril or more — FT

Carlsberg India reported revenue of 87.09 billion rupees for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. The company operates seven breweries and had a 21.9% market share across 16 key states and union territories in fiscal 2026, according to the prospectus.

title: ST Engineering wins initial 'low rate' order for land system platform from defence customer in Europe
article:
Singapore Technologies Engineering has won an initial "low rate" production order for a land systems platform.

The customer is in Europe and the company is hopeful that orders for the full production may follow in the "not too distant" future.

Winning this contract for a land platform is in contrast to other recent overseas defence orders, such as recurring ammunition orders, and more recently, maintenance orders.

ST Engineering's executives, for now, are not saying what kind of product this is, and who the customer is.

However, they stress that this is a significant development.

"This is a validation of the quality and capabilities of our platform and hopefully, the initial vanguard to much larger orders subsequently," says Mervyn Tan, the company's group chief operating officer.

See also: Sats reports 2QFY2027 earnings of $81.1 mil, up 2.8% y-o-y

The key land system platforms built by the company, and which is being marketed around, include various versions of the Terrex family of infantry fighting vehicles, and also the Bronco all-terrain-track-carrier.

Vincent Chong, the company's group president and CEO, points out that this particular platform is also in the run for similar contracts in other markets.

This means if ST Engineering can win orders from other customers as well, it is able to enjoy operational efficiencies.

This aside, in the third quarter of the year, ST Engineering won defence and public security orders worth $1.8 billion, with a total haul of $5.6 billion. Total order book is now at a record level of $37.7 billion.

title: New World considering rights issue as Bain walks away — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): New World Development Co is considering a rights issue to help shore up its finances after Bain Capital decided against investing in the property company, according to people familiar with the situation.

New World may seek to raise as much as HK$25 billion (US$3.2 billion or $4.1 billion) in the potential rights issue, the people said. The indebted developer’s controlling shareholder, the Cheng family, intends to participate and inject fresh capital, the people added, asking not to be identified to discuss private deliberations.

New World’s shares were suspended from trading Friday morning pending an announcement. The shares have fallen 33% this year, leaving the company with a market capitalisation of about HK$12.3 billion.

A rights issue involves a company raising cash by selling new shares to stakeholders at a discount. The banks are considering softly underwriting the share sale, meaning they’ll try to find outside investors instead of promising to buy unsold shares with their own money, the people said.

Deliberations are ongoing and might not result in a rights issue, the people said.

Representatives for New World and the Cheng family didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

See also: Hong Kong listing proceeds hit six-year high, close to record

Bain had been exploring a potential investment in New World but decided against it after failing to agree on terms, people familiar with the situation said, without elaborating. A representative for Bain declined to comment.

Blackstone Inc walked away from a proposed tie-up with New World earlier this year after the Cheng family refused to give up control, Bloomberg News reported in May.

New World reported a record US$3.6 billion ($4.6 billion) fiscal-year loss and has been trying to strengthen its finances after years of liquidity strain caused by the property slump in Hong Kong and mainland China. With significant debt maturing in the coming years, investors are closely focused on its refinancing plans.

See also: New World’s top shareholder seeks bank loan as equity deal looms — Bloomberg

New World chief executive officer Echo Huang told analysts in late September that the developer’s focus was on improving its balance sheet by cutting debt and disposing of assets.

title: US probes if Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): The Justice Department is probing Alice Huang, the woman US officials suspect as a possible spy targeting the ousted head of Nvidia Corp, over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle products made by Super Micro Computer Inc to China, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The previously unreported scrutiny is being led by the US attorney’s office in Manhattan, said the person, who asked not to be identified due to the sensitivity of the matter. It’s unclear whether the probe into Alice Huang is specifically tied to any of the chip smuggling cases already brought by prosecutors in the US or Asia.

The Justice Department is already spearheading an investigation into Alice Huang’s former company Megaspeed International over suspected semiconductor smuggling, Bloomberg News has reported. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.

Of the cases where charges have been brought, the most prominent involves Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, who along with two others Manhattan federal prosecutors charged in March over an alleged conspiracy to send Nvidia — powered servers to an unnamed Southeast Asian company and then divert them to Chinese customers. Super Micro wasn’t named as a defendant and has said it is cooperating with the investigation. Liaw, who pleaded not guilty, is no longer at the company.

Super Micro declined to comment on prosecutors’ scrutiny of Alice Huang before publication. “Supermicro has been responsive to inquiries and has fully cooperated with US and Taiwanese officials, while also voluntarily providing information and engaging with all requests from Singapore authorities to date,” the company said in a subsequent statement. “Megaspeed is not, and has never been, a Supermicro customer. Supermicro maintains a robust compliance programme and continues to work closely with authorities and industry partners to combat diversion and help protect American innovation.”

Spokespeople for the Justice Department and the Manhattan US attorney’s office also declined to comment. It wasn’t immediately clear what potential role Alice Huang, or entities connected to her, could have played in smuggling Super Micro products into China. Justice Department probes can end without any charges being filed.

See also: Elon Musk says it would be an honour to hire Nvidia’s Huang

Alice Huang is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, Bloomberg News has reported, and attempts to reach her were unsuccessful. Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, was in former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s orbit through Megaspeed, the largest buyer of Nvidia’s chips in Southeast Asia, Bloomberg News has reported.

The scrutiny from US prosecutors represents another twist in a rapidly unfolding scandal that has engulfed the booming AI industry. The Justice Department is conducting an espionage probe that includes looking at her relationship with Jensen Huang, said the person familiar with the effort.

No conclusions have been reached by the Justice Department around “who she is or is not” regarding whether Alice Huang acted as a Chinese spy, Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday.

See also: Adani eyes mix of equity, debt for US$2.9 bil Evos takeover — Bloomberg

Jensen Huang’s disclosure on Sunday that he had an extramarital affair plunged Nvidia into an unprecedented crisis, fuelling a sharp selloff in the company’s shares and ultimately his ouster as chief executive officer on Thursday. Jensen is not a target of probes by US law enforcement, according to the person familiar with the matter. Jensen and Alice aren’t related.

Deepening scrutiny into her activities also underscores how Jensen Huang’s admission has reverberated between Silicon Valley, Washington and Beijing. China has rejected the spying allegations as a “smear,” but the episode threatens to emerge as an irritant in a high-stakes upcoming meeting between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping.

Bloomberg News has reported that the unnamed Southeast Asia company referenced in the March indictment was Bangkok-based OBON Corp. OBON hasn’t responded to requests for comment. According to US prosecutors, two unidentified third-party brokers were also involved in diverting servers to China.

“We have taken action against all identified employees and those parties no longer have any relationship with Supermicro,” chief executive officer Charles Liang said in a public letter to stakeholders in March. “Mr Wally Liaw has also resigned from the company’s board of directors.”

Super Micro said in August, following an independent probe, that its current senior management had no knowledge of the alleged scheme.

title: Samsung in talks to acquire data centre cooling firm Modine — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): Samsung Electronics Co is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing Co, a maker of cooling systems for data centres, according to people familiar with the matter.

The companies are discussing a potential transaction that could come together as soon as the coming weeks, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

Modine’s shares closed regular trading Thursday in New York at US$106.10, giving the company a market value of about US$5.6 billion. The stock soared to more than US$135 in late trading, a gain of 28%.

The company’s shares had fallen about 15% since Nov 3, when it reported quarterly results that underwhelmed investors. No final decision has been made and the talks could still fall apart, the people said. Another suitor could also emerge, they added.

The discussions underscore how M&A is picking up around companies that cater to the booming AI market. US companies and their overseas rivals have stepped up efforts to capture the growth opportunity coming from data centres through bigger investments and dealmaking. Among them are Samsung’s Asian rivals Daikin Industries Ltd and LG Electronics Inc, as well as US-based Vertiv Holdings Co.

Representatives for Samsung and Modine declined to comment.

See also: Unilever-McCormick deal facing in-depth review from UK watchdog

Based in Racine, Wisconsin, Modine makes heavy duty cooling and heating systems for large commercial buildings and industrial machines, with its fastest-growing business serving hyperscalers that build data centres. In October, the company spun off its automotive business to focus on its thermal-management operations.

Samsung, with a market value of more than US$900 billion, is one of the largest technology and electronics companies in the world. The Suwon, South Korea-based company’s products include smartphones, televisions, home appliances, thermal solutions and computer memory chips.

While a Modine takeover would be bolder in magnitude, Samsung has been bolstering its thermal solutions offering to data centres through international acquisitions. It purchased Germany-based FläktGroup Holding GmbH for €1.5 billion (US$1.7 billion) last year.

title: Asian stocks gain after Nvidia upheaval, oil holds
article:
(Nov 13): Asian stocks climbed as investors eased back into technology shares amid fading concerns that a leadership crisis at Nvidia Corp may derail the broader artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Oil steadied.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 1%, led by gains in South Korea and Taiwan as shares in regional tech giants Samsung Electronics Co, SK Hynix Inc and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co advanced. US equity-index futures also climbed, with Nasdaq 100 contracts up 0.6% and S&P 500 futures gaining 0.4% after both benchmarks fell Thursday.

Nvidia, the company at the heart of the AI boom, dropped as much as 14% after chief executive officer Jensen Huang was ousted, but dip buyers stepped in, leaving it just 4.3% lower by the close.

Global benchmark Brent crude steadied just below US$96 a barrel after rising Thursday as President Donald Trump said the US could forgo a deal with Iran. Treasury yields mostly held near Thursday’s highs as traders braced for faster Federal Reserve rate hikes, while a gauge of dollar strength was little changed. Gold steadied after a three-session decline and bitcoin traded around US$71,100.

The upheaval at Nvidia is testing the AI trade without derailing the broader investment boom. Instead, it may make investors more selective, favouring companies best placed to benefit from continued spending.

“This is going to be a more differentiated story and players that have stronger balance sheets that are more focused on doing the hard work of that community engagement are likely to be the winners in this next stage of the buildout,” Mike Pyle, deputy head of BlackRock’s Portfolio Management Group, said in an interview on Bloomberg Television.

See also: Asian stocks edge higher, shrug off Nvidia woes

That shift was already evident on Wall Street. Shares of Broadcom Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc, which compete with Nvidia in parts of the AI chip market, rallied over 5% as investors sought potential beneficiaries from the industry leader’s setback.

Nvidia’s market capitalisation briefly dropped below US$4 trillion ($5.2 trillion) with revelations about Huang’s extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, rattling investors ahead of earnings. A related probe into suspected spy Alice Huang and efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer Inc products to China sent that company’s shares down as much as 16%, the most in more than five months.

“Nvidia’s earnings already demand close attention, but they will be under an even brighter spotlight next week,” said Bret Kenwell at eToro. “Investors will be looking to Nvidia for a fresh read on demand and a reason to regain confidence.”

See also: Asian stocks rise on AI enthusiasm, bonds decline

Two other events next week may provide a broader test of appetite for the AI trade: Anthropic PBC’s highly anticipated IPO and CoreWeave Inc’s plan to raise at least US$4 billion through an investment-grade loan offering. Strong institutional demand for Anthropic suggests appetite for AI exposure remains robust.

In Asia, traders will also be watching the yen after it weakened past 160 per dollar for the first time since September, reviving the prospect that Japanese authorities may intervene to support the currency.

“Markets are jittery about potential FX intervention whenever we approach the 160 area,” said Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982.

Higher oil prices added to pressure on Treasuries, extending a sell-off sparked Tuesday by hotter-than-expected inflation and signals that Fed officials may favour more aggressive rate hikes. Policy-sensitive two-year yields edged lower after climbing 14 basis points on Thursday.

On Thursday, New York Fed president John Williams said that US inflation remains high and that policymakers have to take further action to contain price pressures.

“Investors continue to pencil in more rate hikes,” said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US interest rates strategy at TD Securities. While setbacks for US technology shares — which benefited Treasuries last month — “could short-circuit the bearish move at some point, the macro underpinnings are the ones driving Treasuries right now”.

title: Ex-Malaysia digital star that built PM’s avatar is mired in debt
article:
(Nov 13): Earlier this year, Malaysia’s Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) was preparing to list its artificial intelligence unit on Nasdaq and had even built an AI avatar of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Now the onetime digital infrastructure star has lost more than 90% of its market value, is mired in debt and risks defaulting on its Islamic bonds.

Valued at RM10.5 billion (US$2.6 billion) at its peak in 2018, Zetrix’s market capitalisation has plunged to around RM430 million as the company that once held a near-monopoly on providing online state services struggles to diversify its business. Its grip on government contracts began loosening in 2023 as Malaysia shifted away from exclusive concessions to state-run services and competing platforms.

The company’s troubles deepened last month when authorities suspended its remaining online road tolls collection service after saying Zetrix owed the government RM314 million in Road Transport Department fees dating from May 19 to Sept 30.

“We are confident we will weather this,” founder Wong Thean Soon said in an emailed response to questions. “We take a long-term view and understand the market is adjusting to our transition from a primarily Malaysian government-focused business to a more international” one.

In its former guise as MyEG Services Bhd, the company oversaw government online services such as road tax renewals, traffic summons payments and foreign worker permits. As it began losing its exclusive rights to those services, it pivoted to AI and blockchain and started seeking new revenue abroad. It changed its name to Zetrix last year.

See also: Johor property prices rise as demand favours homes near RTS Link

When the value of the company’s stock plunged, Wong was forced to sell 2.22 billion of his Zetrix shares between June and October to meet margin calls on his stock-based loans, ending his role as Zetrix’s largest shareholder. That put the company at risk of breaching its Islamic bonds covenant, which requires Wong to remain Zetrix’s biggest owner.

MARC Ratings subsequently cut the company’s debt score to one rung above default on the risk bondholders could declare a nonpayment. Zetrix, in a filing on Tuesday, said it owed RM25 million in bond payments due Nov 6.

Bursa Malaysia extended its deadline for Zetrix to disclose additional financial information from Wednesday to Nov 13. “The company will take the necessary steps to ensure compliance with the directive within the extended timeframe,” Zetrix said Wednesday.

See also: SoftBank, Grab and PETROS lock in US$1.85 bil seed capital for AI infrastructure in Malaysia

The company’s immediate priorities are to fulfill its obligations and strengthen financial and operational positions, Wong said. Zetrix is banking on its domestic and foreign investments in AI and blockchain to generate new business, he said.

“We endeavor to exceed the previous all-time high because the blockchain and AI growth is still in its nascent stage,” he said of the company’s market value.

Meanwhile, the Anwar avatar that acts as a chatbot for queries from the public has also created complications. The service was indefinitely suspended just days after its July 19 launch when users forced the chatbot to make political statements, some of which were critical of the prime minister.

Wong said Zetrix is working with the premier’s team on new guardrails for the chatbot before reactivating it.

The founder acknowledged that recent developments are weighing on market confidence.

“The group is taking concrete actions and making responsible decisions to reinforce financial discipline, strengthen governance and ensure business continuity,” Wong said.
